classification.classification_note: The fixing commit calls this an out-of-bound vector access, but the saved witness was reproduced under MemorySanitizer and the observable symptom is a use-of-uninitialized-value when `permutateAlt()` indexes a zero-length `state` array with `SIZE_MAX`.

bug_description.original: Project: libsass; Fuzz Target: data_context_fuzzer; Crash Type: Use-of-uninitialized-value; Crash State: std::__1::vector<...>, Sass::ComplexSelector::resolve_parent_refs, Sass::Eval::operator; Sanitizer: memory (MSAN).
bug_description.normalized: A trailing comma in a delayed selector schema makes `parseSelectorList()` append an empty `ComplexSelector` at EOF. Later `resolve_parent_refs()` passes an empty vector to `permutateAlt()`, which underflows `n = in.size() - 1` and reads `state[SIZE_MAX]` from a zero-length allocation.

source.description: First parser-side materialization of the vulnerability-relevant input. Because the outer ruleset selector contains `#{...}`, `parse_ruleset()` takes the delayed selector-schema path and captures the raw selector prefix `4%l:#{&}v,` up to the first `{`, preserving the attacker-controlled trailing comma.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 19-byte ASCII string `4%l:#{&}v,{-#{&}{}}` with no trailing newline. This source step isolates its outer selector text `4%l:#{&}v,`, including the comma that later triggers the EOF reloop.
source.note: The nested block `{-#{&}{}}` is parsed as the ruleset body, but the saved crash occurs while reevaluating the outer selector and before that nested block is expanded.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.code: size_t L = in.size(); size_t n = in.size() - 1; size_t* state = new size_t[L];
root_cause.description: `permutateAlt()` assumes its input vector is non-empty. When `resolve_parent_refs()` passes `vars.size() == 0`, this code underflows `n` to `SIZE_MAX` and allocates a zero-length `state` array without first handling the empty-input case.
root_cause.note: The fixing commit adds the missing obligation immediately before this code: `if (L == 0) return {};`.

sink.description: Crash site. The first loop test in `permutateAlt()` reads `state[n]` even though `state` has length 0 and `n == SIZE_MAX`, which MemorySanitizer reports as a use-of-uninitialized-value.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `src/permutate.hpp:101:11`, with the top stack `permutateAlt -> ComplexSelector::resolve_parent_refs -> Eval::operator()(ComplexSelector*)`.

parser_admitted.description: The stylesheet parser admits the outer ruleset and routes its selector through delayed selector-schema parsing because the selector text contains `#{...}`.

tainted_value_origin.description: First project-side storage of the raw fuzzer-controlled SCSS text.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact ASCII string `4%l:#{&}v,{-#{&}{}}`; this assignment stores that text in the libsass data context for later parsing.

fine_trace.code: memcpy(sass_data, data, size); sass_data[size] = '\0'; struct Sass_Data_Context* ctx = sass_make_data_context(sass_data); sass_compile_data_context(ctx);
fine_trace.note: Harness step. The saved witness is the 19-byte ASCII string `4%l:#{&}v,{-#{&}{}}`; the harness copies it into a NUL-terminated buffer and passes it to libsass through `sass_compile_data_context()`.
The raw SCSS witness from step 0 is stored in project state so the parser later reads the exact attacker-controlled text.

Source. The outer ruleset selector is not directly parsable because it contains `#{...}`, so `parse_ruleset()` captures the raw selector-schema prefix `4%l:#{&}v,` up to the first `{`. The trailing comma is preserved in this delayed selector state.

fine_trace.code: Expression_Obj sel = s->contents()->perform(this); std::string result_str(sel->to_string(options())); result_str = unquote(Util::rtrim(result_str));
fine_trace.note: Evaluating the outer selector schema at the root rule converts it to a concrete selector string. Because there is no original selector on the top-level stack, the interpolated `#{&}` contributes nothing, so `result_str` becomes `4%l:v,` after trimming and unquoting.

The first `parseComplexSelector()` call on `result_str` returns a non-null selector for the prefix before the comma; otherwise line 83 would return the list immediately and the later EOF reloop would be unreachable.
The comma after the first selector is consumed and sets `reloop = true`, so `parseSelectorList()` starts a second loop iteration with the cursor already at end-of-file.

On the second iteration the parser is already at EOF, but this 'superfluous comma' escape only checks `selector_list_delims` (`){};!`), not end-of-file, so the trailing-comma path falls through instead of breaking the loop.

Because step 6 allowed parsing to continue at EOF, `parseComplexSelector()` returns the freshly allocated `sel` from line 20 before any elements are appended. This yields an empty `ComplexSelector` object rather than `nullptr`.
The empty `ComplexSelector` from step 7 is appended as the second selector in the outer `SelectorList`, so the trailing-comma parser artifact becomes persistent AST state.

When `Expand::operator()(Ruleset*)` reevaluates the outer selector list at line 184, this loop still dispatches `operator()` for the second selector from step 8. The saved crash stack contains only one `Expand::operator()(Ruleset*)` frame, matching a crash here before the nested block is expanded.

For this empty top-level complex, `pstack.back()` is the null root selector entry and `elements()` is empty, so neither the parent path nor the element loop adds anything to `vars`. `resolve_parent_refs()` therefore calls `permutateAlt()` with `vars.size() == 0`.

fine_trace.code: size_t L = in.size(); size_t n = in.size() - 1; size_t* state = new size_t[L];
fine_trace.note: Root cause. With the empty input from step 10, `L` is 0, `n` underflows to `SIZE_MAX`, and the function allocates a zero-length `state` array. Vulnerable code has no `if (L == 0) return {};` guard before these operations.
Sink. The first loop condition reads `state[n]` even though `state` has length 0 and `n == SIZE_MAX`. The saved MemorySanitizer run reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at this exact line.

poc.trigger: The saved harness passes the exact ASCII witness `4%l:#{&}v,{-#{&}{}}` into `sass_compile_data_context()`. While expanding the outer ruleset, selector-schema evaluation reparses `4%l:v,`; the trailing comma forces a second `parseSelectorList()` iteration at EOF, appends an empty `ComplexSelector`, and later crashes in `permutateAlt()` when that empty selector is reevaluated.

format.name: Exact ASCII SCSS witness with a trailing-comma outer selector schema
format.contract: The witness is the exact 19-byte ASCII string `4%l:#{&}v,{-#{&}{}}` with no trailing newline. Its outer ruleset selector text ends with a comma immediately before the first `{`; when root-level interpolation removes `#{&}`, `Eval::operator()(Selector_Schema*)` reparses `4%l:v,`, and `parseSelectorList()` performs one more loop at EOF and appends an empty `ComplexSelector`.
